statement: Let n = len(s). Whenever the call returns Result.ok r, r is the largest integer L with 0 <= L <= n such that either L = 0, or there exist integers i and j with 0 <= i < j, i+L <= n, j+L <= n, and for every k with 0 <= k < L, s[i+k] = s[j+k]. Equivalently, r is 0 if no nonempty contiguous substring of s occurs at two distinct starting positions; otherwise r is the maximum length of a nonempty contiguous substring of s that occurs at two distinct starting positions (the two occurrences may overlap).
preconditions: Let n = len(s). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, the byte s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122).

statement: For every s satisfying the preconditions, the call longest_repeating_substring(s) returns Result.ok r for some I64 value r; it does not fail (no overflow, out-of-bounds indexing, or panic).
preconditions: Let n = len(s). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, the byte s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122).

statement: Let n = len(s). Whenever the call returns Result.ok r, 0 <= r <= n-1. In particular r < n.
preconditions: Let n = len(s). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, the byte s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122).

statement: Let n = len(s). Whenever the call returns Result.ok r with r > 0, there exist integers i and j with 0 <= i < j, i+r <= n, j+r <= n, and for every k with 0 <= k < r, s[i+k] = s[j+k]. Thus a length-r contiguous substring actually occurs at two distinct starting positions.
preconditions: Let n = len(s). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, the byte s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122).

statement: Let n = len(s). Whenever the call returns Result.ok r, for every integer L with 0 <= L <= n and every pair of integers i and j with 0 <= i < j, i+L <= n, j+L <= n, if s[i+k] = s[j+k] for every k with 0 <= k < L, then L <= r. Equivalently, no contiguous substring of length greater than r occurs at two distinct starting positions.
preconditions: Let n = len(s). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, the byte s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122).

statement: Let n = len(s). Whenever the call returns Result.ok r, for every integer L with 1 <= L <= n-1, the following are equivalent: (a) L <= r; (b) there exist integers i and j with 0 <= i < j, i+L <= n, j+L <= n, and s[i+k] = s[j+k] for every k with 0 <= k < L. In words, the set of positive repeated lengths is exactly {1, 2, ..., r}, empty when r = 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(s). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, the byte s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122).

statement: Let n = len(s). Whenever the call returns Result.ok r, r = 0 if and only if for every pair of indices i and j with 0 <= i < j < n, s[i] != s[j]. Equivalently, r > 0 if and only if some byte value occurs at least twice in s.
preconditions: Let n = len(s). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, the byte s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122).

statement: Let n = len(s). Whenever the call returns Result.ok r, for every integer interval [a,b] with 0 <= a <= b < n such that s[t] = s[a] for every t with a <= t <= b, if k = b-a+1, then r >= k-1. In particular, a contiguous run of k identical bytes forces a repeated substring of length k-1.
preconditions: Let n = len(s). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, the byte s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122).

statement: Let n = len(s). Whenever the call returns Result.ok r, for every integer L with 1 <= L < n such that s[k] = s[n-L+k] for every k with 0 <= k < L (i.e. a proper prefix of s of length L equals the suffix of s of length L), we have r >= L.
preconditions: Let n = len(s). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, the byte s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122).

statement: Let n = len(s). Define rev(s) to be the length-n byte slice with rev(s)[i] = s[n-1-i] for every i with 0 <= i < n. If the call on s returns Result.ok r and the call on rev(s) returns Result.ok r', then r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(s). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, the byte s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122).

statement: Let n = len(s). Let t be any byte slice of length n that also satisfies the lowercase precondition (1 <= n <= 2000 and all its bytes are in 97..122). Suppose that for all indices p and q with 0 <= p < q < n, s[p] = s[q] if and only if t[p] = t[q]. If the call on s returns Result.ok r and the call on t returns Result.ok r', then r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(s). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, the byte s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122).

statement: Let n = len(s). For any integers a and b with 0 <= a <= b < n, let t be the contiguous substring of s defined by len(t) = b-a+1 and t[k] = s[a+k] for 0 <= k < len(t). If the call on s returns Result.ok r and the call on t returns Result.ok r_t, then r_t <= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(s). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, the byte s[i] is a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[i] <= 122).
